root_cause.text: In `drm/gma500/oaktrail_lvds_init()`, the error path unconditionally destroyed the connector’s DDC I2C adapter even when it came from `i2c_get_adapter()`, so a late init failure attempted to unregister an already-registered adapter while an extra reference was still held, causing the teardown to hang waiting for that reference to drop.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit notes that the init code first calls `i2c_get_adapter()` and later may allocate/register its own adapter, but “the error handling does not separate these cases,” and the patch fixes this by initializing `ddc_bus` to `NULL` and only calling `gma_i2c_destroy(ddc_bus)` when `ddc_bus` is not `ERR_OR_NULL`, instead of always destroying `connector->ddc`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize `ddc_bus` to NULL to avoid using an uninitialized pointer during LVDS setup.
intent_record.what: The local variable `ddc_bus` in `oaktrail_lvds_init()` was changed from an uninitialized pointer declaration to an initialized pointer declaration set to `NULL`.
intent_record.how: This ensures `ddc_bus` has a defined value before any conditional assignment or use, preventing accidental use of an indeterminate pointer if no DDC bus is assigned during initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the oaktrail LVDS initialization error path to safely destroy the DDC bus only when it was successfully created.
intent_record.what: The error path in `oaktrail_lvds_init()` was changed from unconditionally calling `gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc))` to conditionally calling `gma_i2c_destroy(ddc_bus)` only when `ddc_bus` is not an error pointer or NULL.
intent_record.how: This prevents the cleanup code from attempting to destroy an invalid or uninitialized I2C/DDC bus reference during failure handling, avoiding crashes or undefined behavior on the error path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the oaktrail LVDS initialization error path to safely destroy the DDC bus only when it was successfully created.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix oaktrail LVDS initialization error handling so the DDC bus pointer is safely initialized and only destroyed if it was successfully created.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the oaktrail LVDS init error path and the DDC I2C adapter teardown logic, which matches the reported bug of unconditionally destroying an adapter obtained via i2c_get_adapter().

candidates.rationale: This error-path cleanup unconditionally destroys the connector's DDC I2C adapter. If the adapter came from i2c_get_adapter(), it was only borrowed/registered elsewhere and should not be destroyed here, which can trigger the teardown hang described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the old error path that unconditionally destroyed the connector's DDC I2C adapter even when it came from i2c_get_adapter(). In this snippet, that old behavior is no longer present. The error path now uses the connector's actual adapter pointer: `connector->ddc = i2c_adap;` and on failure it calls `gma_i2c_destroy(to_gma_i2c_chan(connector->ddc));` after `mutex_unlock(&dev->mode_config.mutex);`. The previous logic `if (gma_encoder->ddc_bus) { gma_i2c_destroy(gma_encoder->ddc_bus); gma_encoder->ddc_bus = NULL; }` is removed. This shows the cleanup was reworked so the adapter is tracked from `drm_connector` and not torn down via the old encoder field, which is the fix for the hang described.
